question: Why does the public site show 15 October matches when the workflow publishes a verified snapshot every four hours?
answer: GitHub Pages for this repository is in legacy build mode and publishes the checked-in branch root on every push to main. The refreshed site is uploaded as a workflow artifact under the same paths, so the two publishers race and whichever lands last wins. On 2026-10-22 the legacy build for 2fb99b0 landed after the artifact and the public site reverted to the 15 October root.

evidence.claim: The public site is the branch root, not the workflow artifact.
evidence.method: GET https://buffedlizard55-lab.github.io/MaltaProj3/data/row-source-audit.json and compare with the tracked file

evidence.claim: The public snapshot is six days old and every row in it has already started.
evidence.result: identical to the tracked data/latest.json committed on 15 October

evidence.claim: Pages serves the branch root in legacy mode.
The legacy build finished eight minutes after the push and republished the root.
The refresh run for the same commit had not deployed yet when the root was republished.
The workflow token cannot switch the Pages source to the workflow builder.
A complete, newer snapshot already exists inside the repository.
evidence.result: It cannot be rebuilt locally because validate.py refuses a snapshot whose inventory_observed_at does not match data/evidence/hotspawn-context.json, and that evidence is produced by the collector on the runner. The workflow must be the publisher.

evidence.claim: The four-hour refresh was being cancelled while pending, before it could start.
evidence.method: gh run list --workflow=pages.yml and gh api repos/.../actions/runs/<id>

observed.mechanism: GitHub cancels a pending run when a newer run enters the same concurrency group; cancel-in-progress:false only governs the in-progress run.

fix.summary: Publish the verified build into the branch root from inside the four-hour workflow, so both publishers serve the same current site.
guards: refuses a build whose index.html is smaller than 50 kB (a redirect stub)
refuses a missing or unparseable data/latest.json
refuses a snapshot older than 12 hours unless --allow-stale is passed
refuses to publish a snapshot older than the one already in the root
writes only files whose bytes changed, so a re-run is a no-op
the workflow step runs only after the deploy and public-site verification steps succeed
scheduled and manual refreshes use their own concurrency group, so pushes can no longer cancel them while pending
fix.published_paths: every rendered page, assets/, data/latest.json, data/origination.json, data/sources.json, data/row-source-audit.json, data/origination/aliases.json, data/evidence/hotspawn-fixtures.json, data/evidence/hotspawn-context.json, .nojekyll
fix.excluded_paths: data/research/ (19 MB) and the remaining data/evidence/ attachments (3 MB) - they change every refresh and are still served by the artifact deploy

limitations: The Pages source cannot be switched from a workflow token (403), so this repository keeps two publishers. The fix makes them agree instead of removing one.

Bulk evidence attachments in the branch root are refreshed by their own sessions, not every four hours. During a legacy-build window, a row's saved-evidence link can therefore show an older response while the row itself is current.
A workflow push that carries [skip ci] does not start another workflow run, but the legacy Pages build still runs for it - which is what republishes the root.
